title: Phasing In a Business Security Deposit Rise from Load Growth
content:
A rise in the requirement of a held business Security Deposit driven by recent load growth is phased in against the held amount.

**Held amount.** The cash received on the deposit less the cash refunded from it, plus the interest credited on the deposit.

**Rule.** Where the billing basis of the recalculation is the recent mean (the mean of the regular bills issued in the 3 months ending on the recalculation date):
- if the requirement before rounding exceeds the held amount by more than 1 times the held amount, only 0.5 (one half) of that excess is added to the held amount;
- if the requirement before rounding exceeds the held amount by no more than 1 times it, 0.75 (three quarters) of the excess is added.

Otherwise the requirement before rounding is taken in full.

| Billing basis is the recent mean | Excess of the requirement before rounding over the held amount | Phased amount |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | More than the held amount | Held amount plus one half of the excess |
| Yes | Above zero, up to the held amount | Held amount plus three quarters of the excess |
| Yes | None | Requirement before rounding |
| No | Any | Requirement before rounding |

## Cases (hypothetical deposit: cash received USD 3900.00, nothing refunded, interest credited USD 100.00, so a held amount of USD 4000.00)

| Basis is the recent mean | Requirement before rounding (USD) | Excess (USD) | Phased amount (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | 9000.00 | 5000.00 (more than 4000.00) | 4000.00 plus 2500.00, which is 6500.00 |
| Yes | 7000.00 | 3000.00 | 4000.00 plus 2250.00, which is 6250.00 |
| No | 7000.00 | 3000.00 | 7000.00 |
